blocks.text: “A PROPHETESS, THE DAUGHTER OF PHANUEL, OF THE TRIBE OF ASER” (LUKE 2:36) · NEW TESTAMENT
Anna. A widow who served God in the temple night and day, and spoke of the child to all who looked for redemption.
SCRIPTURE CALLS
Prophetess
ERA
New Testament AD 1–60
IN THE DAYS OF
Augustus · Herod the Great
BOOK
None bears the name
HOW THE WORD CAME
Luke calls her “a prophetess” but records none of her words.
THE CALL
How the word came
From the textLuke calls her “a prophetess” but records none of her words. Luke 2:36–38
She had lived with a husband seven years, and was a widow who “departed not from the temple, but served God with fastings and prayers night and day.” Luke 2:36–37
Coming in at the same moment as Simeon spoke, she “gave thanks likewise unto the Lord”. Luke 2:38

Before two rulers

HOW THE STORY ENDS
Scripture says, tradition says
SCRIPTURE SAYS

TRADITION SAYS

OPEN QUESTIONS
Where readers have differed
She was about 84 years old
Albert Barnes; J. A. Bengel (1742); most, according to A. B. Bruce (1897)

Barnes: “she was about 84 years of age. It does not mean that she had been a widow for that long time.” Bengel: “These were the years of her whole life, not of her widowhood only.” Luke 2:37 [32][34][35]
She had been a widow for 84 years
John Gill (1746–1748); E. H. Plumptre (Ellicott’s commentary, about 1878); Godet (as reported by Bruce, 1897)

Gill: the number is “not the date of her whole age … but of her widowhood state”. Plumptre follows the manuscripts that read “up to the point of fourscore and four years” and, supposing her married at fifteen, reckons her age at 106. Vincent (1887) notes that “the best texts” read “until” where the KJV has “about”, which makes the number her years as a widow. Luke 2:36–37 [33][31][35][36]

WHAT SCRIPTURE DOES NOT SAY
Luke records none of Anna’s words.
Scripture does not name her husband or say how he died.
